sources.title: How To Apply for NC Medicaid (NC DHHS)
sources.supports: Claim-verification note (HACK-17): page retrieved 2026-10-30; the page displays 'last modified 10/08/2026'. Verified on this page: the four application channels (online ePASS, in person at a local DSS, by phone, by mail/email/fax/drop-off); the 'apply at any time of the year' statement; the suggestion that people who are not sure if they are eligible should apply anyway; the required-application-info list (full legal name and date of birth for at least one person applying, a mailing address for at least one person applying, and a signature); the documents table quoted in required_documents; the decision timeline (up to 45 days for DSS to decide, up to 90 days for disability applications); and the link to the DHB-5200 printable application PDF.

sources.title: DHB-5200 Application for Health Coverage (NC DHHS policies)
sources.supports: Claim-verification note (HACK-17): PDF retrieved 2026-10-30 from the printable-application link on medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/apply; form revision IA-9-2020 per the file name and the form footer. DHB-5200 vs DHB-5201 reconciliation: the official apply page presents DHB-5200 as the printable application for the household health-coverage journey and DHB-5201-ia as the 'short form' for a single adult with no dependents and no employer health coverage; the demo journey is the INITIAL MAGI Medicaid application for a household, so DHB-5200 governs. The form's own words (Step 1 and its SSN note) support the home-address-may-be-blank and SSN-optional claims recorded in rules.

sources.title: Mecklenburg County Department of Community Resources — Apply for Benefits
sources.supports: Claim-verification note (HACK-17): page retrieved 2026-10-30. Verified on this page: Mecklenburg County residents apply for Medicaid online through North Carolina ePASS (or Mecklenburg County All Access), return paper applications in person at the county Community Resource Centers (each with a 24-hour secure document drop-off box), fax applications to the county fax number published on the page, or apply by phone through the Economic Services Call Center. County channels may change — re-verify before relying on a specific address, fax number, or phone number.

items: NC Medicaid eligibility is decided by the Department of Social Services under the program's official rules — never by this app.
You can apply at any time of the year, per the official application guidance.
The official guidance says that if you are not sure whether you are eligible, they suggest you apply anyway.

This entry covers the initial Medicaid application for a household (the DHB-5200 health-coverage application). The DHB-5201 'short form' is the official alternative for a single adult with no dependents and no employer health coverage.
No income limits or eligibility thresholds are stated in this entry: the official eligibility guidance decides them, and the application form's examples are not treated as current limits.
The application's home-address field may be left blank if you don't have one — the form prints that instruction next to the field — and a mailing address can be listed separately.
Family members who don't need health coverage do not have to provide an immigration status or Social Security Number, per the application's own instructions.
Full legal name and date of birth for at least one person applying, and a mailing address for at least one person applying.
Your signature on the application — written, voice, or digital depending on how you apply.

If you have them, copies of documents for: North Carolina residency (a photo ID with your address, a utility bill, a lease or mortgage agreement, a vehicle registration, or employment documentation — or the application's 'NC Residency Declaration' box if you have no document).
Income documents if employed: pay stubs, employer verification, or your most recent tax return; if self-employed: your most recent tax return or copies of your business records.
Date of birth: a photo ID with your date of birth listed, or a birth certificate.
Social Security Number: a copy of your Social Security card or proof you applied for one, another official document with your name and SSN, or a military ID card.
Citizenship: a birth certificate or a passport. Immigration status for non-U.S. citizens: a copy of your visa/immigration card.
The official page says including copies of the documents you have may speed up the process, and that not all documents apply to everyone.

items.label: Apply online through ePASS (an NCID is required)
How to apply for NC Medicaid (official application guidance)
When to apply
items.due: Any time of the year — the official application guidance states you can apply at any time.

items.label: Decision timeline after you apply
items.due: The official page states it can take up to 45 days for the Department of Social Services to decide, and up to 90 days for disability applications — an agency processing timeline, not a promise about any case.

items: Pick a channel: apply online through ePASS, in person at your local Department of Social Services, over the phone, or by mail, email, fax, or drop-off.
If you apply on paper, download, print, and fill out the DHB-5200 application first.
Include copies of the documents you have — the official page says it may speed up the process.
Sign the application — the official guidance reminds applicants not to forget to sign.
After you apply, the agency may contact you for more information, so keep the address and phone number on the application correct.
